title: Anthropic Outlines Its AI-Powered Code Review Process for Claude Code
gist: Anthropic's Claude Code team describes a layered, risk-based code review process for AI-generated code: pre-PR agent verification, multi-agent automated review and security gating, and human approvals scaled by risk. Merged PRs more than doubled June-September while reverts fell over 40%, and first-round pass rates rose from 65% to 78%.

insights.claim: Between June and September, merged pull requests to Anthropic's Claude Code repository more than doubled while the share of changes requiring a revert fell by over 40%.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Evidence that AI-heavy development can scale output without degrading quality, supporting the agentic coding productivity thesis.
insights.locator: Between June and September, merged pull requests

insights.claim: After Anthropic capped and refocused automated review cycles, the share of internal pull requests passing after one review-and-fix round rose from 65% to 78%, and those needing five or more rounds dropped from 8.9% to 1.5%.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Review-loop design, not just model quality, drives agentic coding efficiency; a differentiator for AI code-review products.
insights.locator: These adjustments have improved review efficiency

insights.claim: Anthropic's Claude Code team shifts verification before the pull request: Claude runs tests, builds and linters, and a separate agent reviews changes in a fresh context.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Fresh-context self-review is a reusable pattern; signals demand for agent-integrated CI tooling.
insights.locator: Rather than relying on traditional line-by-line reviews

insights.claim: Every Claude Code pull request passes through Claude-powered reviewers where multiple agents independently investigate potential bugs before another group verifies the findings, and a separate security review can block merges.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Multi-agent review with verification layers raises compute consumption per PR, supportive of inference demand.
insights.locator: Every pull request then goes through several automated checks

insights.claim: To prevent automated reviewers from generating excessive feedback, Anthropic caps review cycles at three rounds before asking the author to reconsider the implementation, and later reviews only examine new changes.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Bounding AI review loops is key to controlling cost and developer friction in agentic workflows.
insights.locator: The team also introduced mechanisms to prevent

insights.claim: Anthropic feeds incidents and reverted changes into a growing evaluation dataset to measure and improve its automated code reviewers, and releases merged changes behind feature flags with gradual rollouts.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Production incident data as eval fuel creates a compounding advantage for vendors running AI review at scale.
insights.locator: Anthropic's approach extends beyond code review itself

insights.claim: Anthropic scales human approval by change risk: low-risk changes like docs or flagged internal features may need no human approval, medium-risk need one, high-risk need two, and sensitive areas like CI workflows always require human oversight.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: A template for enterprises adopting AI coding agents; reduces the human review bottleneck that limits AI coding ROI.
insights.locator: Human involvement depends on the risk

insights.claim: In Anthropic's process, humans remain responsible for architecture, product direction, high-risk changes and final outcomes, and the person directing an AI agent stays accountable for the code it produces.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Accountability stays with humans, implying AI coding augments rather than fully replaces engineers in the near term.

insights.claim: Anthropic's approach optimizes code review around the risk a change introduces rather than how much code a human has personally read, implying teams must rebalance automated verification and human oversight as AI-generated code grows.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Shift in software process economics; watch for QA/testing and code-review tooling consolidation.
insights.locator: The central idea is to optimize code review

insights.claim: Commentators question whether AI-driven code review is effectively becoming testing, blurring the boundaries between software engineering, testing and QA teams.
insights.speaker: Robert Krzaczyński
insights.so_what: Potential organizational restructuring of QA functions as AI review absorbs testing roles.
insights.quote: So code review is officially synonymous with testing now? Should the code review mechanism be owned by QA team? Is there still a QA team?
